item.title: Democratic socialist Francesca Hong loses Wisconsin governor’s primary despite leading in polls, a setback for the surging movement
item.description: Hong, a state lawmaker and former restaurant owner, narrowly lost to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley after an unexpectedly close primary. She had promised to put a hold on building data centers, impose higher taxes on millionaires and set up public grocery stores.

item.title: State Rep. Lisa Demuth defeats Trump-endorsed Mike Lindell in Minnesota gubernatorial primary. She will face Sen. Amy Klobuchar.
item.description: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz (D) set the governor’s race abuzz when he announced in January that he would not seek a third term in the wake of a welfare-fraud investigation in the state that has drawn the national spotlight.

item.title: Michael Alfonso wins Wisconsin GOP primary for House seat once held by his father-in-law, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy
item.description: President Donald Trump backed Alfonso, holding a telephone town hall for the 26-year-old and branding him a “MAGA warrior.”

item.title: Rep. John B. Larson loses bid for 15th term in Connecticut, becoming latest Democratic incumbent to fall to younger opponent
item.description: The 78-year-old Larson is the latest lawmaker to lose reelection this year as Democratic primary voters across the country choose younger candidates while ousting five House incumbents over the age of 65. The winner, former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin, received the state party’s endorsement over Larson in an upset at the May convention.

item.title: Rep. Ralph Norman to face Darline Graham in Republican runoff for the Senate seat held by the late Lindsey Graham
item.description: Norman and Graham will now go head-to-head in the Aug. 25 runoff. Many conservative activists in South Carolina have said they disagreed with President Donald Trump’s decision to endorse Darline Graham, citing her lack of experience or voting record.

item.title: Darline Graham advances to a GOP runoff in the race to replace her late brother, Lindsey Graham, in the Senate
item.description: The whirlwind race, taking place exactly a month after Lindsey Graham unexpectedly died, drew a crowded field of Republican challengers in South Carolina, despite President Donald Trump endorsing Darline Graham.

item.title: Today’s tweens have less independence, costing parents more in babysitting
item.description: While some youngsters are working as babysitters, others are still being babysat. The changing norms are costing parents.

item.description: New details of how ChatGPT maker OpenAI failed to notice that its models had launched a hacking spree raise questions about the industry’s approach to safety. Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle and state law enforcement officials across the country have called for new scrutiny and regulation of the industry.

item.title: Death toll rising after 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Colombia, with at least 111 people killed
item.description: Rescue workers were searching for survivors in the rubble of fallen buildings in several cities. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said 61 buildings collapsed and 52 schools, 18 health centers, 17 community centers and six airports were affected.

item.title: Trump nominates loyalist to office that would oversee Reflecting Pool investigation
item.description: Dennis Kirk, a Project 2025 author who had worked for then-Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, may now run the Interior Department’s inspector general office.

item.description: The president has pushed to narrow which vaccines are administered to children and split shots into multiple appointments.

item.description: Lawmakers are calling for protections after incidents in 12 states. An EPA rule that Republicans fought would “remove most of the low-hanging fruit,” a cybersecurity expert said.

item.title: 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Colombia kills at least 20 and destroys buildings in multiple cities
item.description: The temblor, which struck Colombia’s Pacific coast shortly after 8:30 a.m., also shook Ecuador. There was no tsunami threat, Colombia’s General Maritime Directorate said.
